title: Nested list/dict reasoning payloads are dropped inside dict fields
reasoning: _extract_string_content claims to extract strings from list and dict payload shapes, but when it handles a dict it only returns nested values that are already strings. It does not recurse into dict fields whose values are lists or nested dicts. As a result, a reasoning content block such as {"type":"reasoning","content":[{"text":"..."}]} or {"type":"thinking","reasoning_details":[...]} reaches _extract_string_content(block) and returns None even though the same helper can extract from a list when the list is passed directly. Providers often wrap reasoning text in content/details arrays, so these thinking deltas can be silently omitted from the stream.
recommendation: In the dict branch of _extract_string_content, call _extract_string_content(nested) for each supported key and return the first non-empty result, instead of accepting only direct strings.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and the excerpt has no regression coverage for structured reasoning blocks with nested list or dict content.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for extract_thinking_content with a delta containing content=[{"type":"reasoning","content":[{"text":"hidden reasoning"}]}] and assert it returns "hidden reasoning".
